name: Lenses
description: Configures the parallel-lens dispatch SWE uses when TPM runs Review Mode or Planning Mode.

reviewLenses.label: Review Mode Lenses
reviewLenses.description: Comma-separated list of review lenses. SWE-1 runs the first, SWE-2 the second, etc. See the keyword table below for available lenses.

planningLenses.label: Planning Mode Lenses
planningLenses.description: Comma-separated list of planning lenses. Each becomes one SWE producing a plan fragment. See the keyword table below for available lenses.

autoKickReviewOnColleagueBranch.label: Auto-Kick Review On Colleague Branch
autoKickReviewOnColleagueBranch.description: When on, TPM inspects branch authorship at session start and auto-kicks Review Mode (security/logic/quality lens dispatch) if every commit on the current branch was authored by someone other than the current user. Useful for reviewers who routinely pull down colleague branches for code review and want the lens dispatch ready before they ask. Off requires the user to manually request Review Mode. Default off so the trigger is opt-in and does not surprise users on fresh installs.

autoKickPlanningOnFreshBranch.label: Auto-Kick Planning On Fresh Branch
autoKickPlanningOnFreshBranch.description: When on, TPM inspects commit count at session start and auto-kicks Planning Mode (architecture/implementation/test-strategy lens dispatch) if the current branch has zero commits ahead of its base. Useful for users who start sessions on freshly-created branches and want a planning pass before any work happens. Off requires the user to manually request Planning Mode. Default off for the same reason as the review trigger.

triggerBaseBranch.label: Trigger Base Branch
triggerBaseBranch.description: The reference branch the planning trigger compares against when counting commits ahead. Common values are main, master, or develop depending on the project's main-line branch name. Set this once per project to match the team's convention. Has no effect when Auto-Kick Planning On Fresh Branch is off.

mixedAuthorBehavior.label: Mixed Author Behavior
mixedAuthorBehavior.description: How the review trigger handles a branch where SOME commits are by the current user and others are by colleagues. ask prompts the user to confirm whether this is a review session or their own work, useful for collaborators who routinely co-author branches. skip silently treats mixed branches as author-mode and does not kick Review Mode. kick treats any colleague commit as a review trigger and kicks immediately, useful for solo reviewers who never co-author. Default ask is the safest middle ground.
